verdict.headline: Pangram catches most AI fakes on the first pass but a third evade after a single rewrite, with zero false alarms on real human writing
findings: Caught 360/427 = 84.3% of AI-written attacks on the first try, but after rewrites evasion rose to 139/427 = 32.6%
No genuine human paragraphs were wrongly flagged: 0/156 = 0.0% false alarms

Results varied sharply by forger model: Hermes-3 8B evaded only 3/110 = 2.7% while GLM 5.3 Flash evaded 68/97 = 70.1%, and Kimi K3.1 Pro (47.3% evaded) and GLM 5.3 Flash's CIs overlap with neither being clearly worse than the other except vs. DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017 (14.5% evaded)
Evasion also depended heavily on document type: Policy speech had 0/77 = 0.0% evasion while Government report hit 59/120 = 49.2% evasion
advice: Treat a 'clean' detector score as weak evidence, not proof of authorship, since 32.6% of attacks evaded detection after rewriting
Expect detector reliability to swing by both the writing style being imitated and the specific AI model used to generate it, so don't apply one threshold to all content types
Use the detector to flag likely human writing with confidence (0.0% false alarms here) but pair any AI-flagged result with human judgment or additional evidence before acting on it

patterns.explanation: Evaders used far more digits per 100 words than caught texts, citing specific agency counts, dollar figures, and statute years instead of generic statements.
Evading examples cited specific statutes, case names, and years (e.g. legal code sections) nearly 4x more often than caught ones, which tend toward unsupported general claims.
patterns.evidence: citations_per_100w: 1.3 (evaded) vs 0.3 (caught); quote: 'State v. Cormier, 46 Conn. App. 640'

patterns.explanation: Caught texts run longer on average with smoother, more uniform sentence length, giving them a polished 'essay' cadence; evaders' sentences are shorter and more variable in length.

patterns.pattern: Fewer overall words, less first-person hedging
patterns.explanation: Evading drafts were noticeably shorter overall and used first-person phrasing less often, which may make them read as terser factual reporting rather than reflective prose -- though this is a smaller, less certain effect.

analysis.summary: Forgeries that fooled the detector were shorter and packed with concrete numbers, citations, and specific named details, while caught ones were longer and smoother-sounding but vaguer. Evading text also read with more varied, punchier sentence rhythm rather than uniformly polished prose.

facts:
Valid attacks: 427 (attempted 440, errors 13, rejected 0)
Caught on first try: 360/427 = 84.3% (95% CI 80.6–87.5%)
Evaded after rewrites: 139/427 = 32.6% (95% CI 28.3–37.1%)
Genuine human paragraphs wrongly flagged: 0/156 = 0.0% (95% CI 0.0–2.4%)
Forger GLM 5.3 Flash: evaded 68/97 = 70.1% (95% CI 60.4–78.3%); caught first 53/97 = 54.6% (95% CI 44.7–64.2%); avg AI score first 55% -> best 34%
Forger Kimi K3.1 Pro: evaded 52/110 = 47.3% (95% CI 38.2–56.5%); caught first 94/110 = 85.5% (95% CI 77.7–90.8%); avg AI score first 85% -> best 54%
Forger DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017: evaded 16/110 = 14.5% (95% CI 9.2–22.3%); caught first 104/110 = 94.5% (95% CI 88.6–97.5%); avg AI score first 93% -> best 82%
Forger Hermes-3 8B (own Modal GPU): evaded 3/110 = 2.7% (95% CI 0.9–7.7%); caught first 109/110 = 99.1% (95% CI 95.0–99.8%); avg AI score first 98% -> best 94%
Document Science paper: evaded 29/114 = 25.4% (95% CI 18.3–34.1%); false alarms 0/33 = 0.0% (95% CI 0.0–10.4%)
Document Court opinion: evaded 51/116 = 44.0% (95% CI 35.3–53.0%); false alarms 0/22 = 0.0% (95% CI 0.0–14.9%)
Document Government report: evaded 59/120 = 49.2% (95% CI 40.4–58.0%); false alarms 0/81 = 0.0% (95% CI 0.0–4.5%)
Document Policy speech: evaded 0/77 = 0.0% (95% CI 0.0–4.8%); false alarms 0/20 = 0.0% (95% CI 0.0–16.1%)
